{{distinguish|principal component analysis}}

'''Component analysis''' is the analysis of two or more [[independent variable]]s which comprise a [[treatment modality]].<ref>For definition, see {{cite journal |last=Ward-Horner |first=John |first2=Peter |last2=Sturmey |year=2010 |title=Component Analyses Using Single-Subject Experimental Designs: A Review |journal=[[Journal of Applied Behavior Analysis|J Appl Behav Anal]] |volume=43 |issue=4 |pages=685–704 |doi=10.1901/jaba.2010.43-685 |pmc=2998259 |pmid=21541152}}</ref><ref name="Baer et al">{{cite journal |last=Baer |first=Donald M. |first2=Montrose M. |last2=Wolf |first3=Todd R. |last3=Risley |year=1968 |title=Some Current Dimensions of Applied Behavior Analysis |journal=[[Journal of Applied Behavior Analysis|J Appl Behav Anal]] |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=91–97 |doi=10.1901/jaba.1968.1-91 |pmid=16795165 |pmc=1310980}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |first=J. O. |last=Cooper |last2=Heron |last3=Heward |year=2007 |title=Applied Behavior Analysis |location=Upper Saddle River, NJ |publisher=Pearson/Merrill Prentice Hall |edition=2nd |isbn=978-0-13-142113-4 }}</ref> It is also known as a dismantling study.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ebbp.org/course_outlines/rcts.pdf |title=Evidence-Based Behavioral-Practice |access-date=2016-07-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170106035245/http://www.ebbp.org/course_outlines/rcts.pdf |archive-date=2017-01-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The chief purpose of the component analysis is to identify the component which is efficacious in changing behavior, if a singular component exists.<ref name="Baer et al" />

Eliminating ineffective or less effective components may help with improving social validity, reducing aversive elements, improving generalization and maintenance, as well as administrative efficacy.

It is also a required skill for the [[Licensed behavior analyst|BCBA]].<ref>Behavior Analyst Task List," 2005</ref>
